why: The student says StdDraw.point(256, 256) draws in the middle because it 'uses pixels'. That is the PixelCoordinates misconception: the default scale is the unit square, so the point is far outside the window and only the square centred at (0.5, 0.5) shows.

concepts.quote: the point uses pixels, so both are in the middle
concepts.why: This is the wrong rule that point(256, 256) is the middle of the default window. Coordinates are in the unit square, so the point cannot be seen.
No scale is set, so the default unit square applies, not a 0 to 512 pixel range.

concepts.quote: The square uses 0.5 as the centre
concepts.why: It correctly says the square is centred on (x, y) but says nothing about its size, half-side 0.25 (side 0.5).
The answer makes no claim about double values.
